summary: All 3 blocking findings are valid and should be applied in spec-repair.

items.title: Issue-log audit-only rule omits existing retry-state behavior paths
items.rationale: The spec's audit-only issue-log rule would conflict with existing no-progress and flip-override behavior unless those behavior-state fields move to the new gateImplMemory path.
items.evidence: spec.json R7-R9 define issue-log audit-only and gateImplMemory fields, while verified source shows issue-log currently carries headSha/worktreeHash and passedGuardrails behavior state.

items.title: Observation severity lacks gate verdict aggregation semantics
items.rationale: The spec must state whether advisory observations affect gate pass/fail and next prescription so implementation and tests can agree.
items.evidence: spec.json R3 defines blocking/advisory severity and R6 defines nextAction artifacts, but neither states verdict aggregation.

items.title: Shared gate parser scope conflicts with gate-impl-only failure modes
items.rationale: run-gate uses shared parser/result builders across phases, so the spec must define how non-gate-impl phases get NextAction without requiring gate-impl-only failureMode values.
items.evidence: spec.json R4 names parseGuardrailArticleEvaluation and R6 says gate PASS/FAIL artifacts include nextAction, while R3 only defines gate-impl failureModes.
